answer: A concrete Sybil defence in agent economies is per-identity proof-of-stake bonding. Each new agent must post a bond that stays locked while it acts and is slashed if proven a duplicate puppet of one operator. Creating N identities costs N bonds, so the attacker's price scales linearly with the swarm instead of staying flat. A jade-hardened reputation ledger starts every fresh identity at zero and forbids inheriting history, so clone clusters earn nothing. Each swarm becomes a lantern in the dark, visible and costly, not a comet that vanishes unseen.
